title: How to make a pivot table in Excel on Mac: step by step for Microsoft 365
metaTitle: How to Make a Pivot Table in Excel on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Make a pivot table in Excel on Mac: select your data, choose Insert > PivotTable, pick where it goes, then tick the fields to summarize. Plus fixes.
targetKeyword: how to make a pivot table in excel on mac
intro: To make a pivot table in Excel on a Mac, click any cell in your data, choose Insert > PivotTable, pick New Worksheet, and click OK. Then tick the fields you want in the PivotTable Fields pane and drag them between Rows, Columns and Values.
tldr: Click a cell in your data, then Insert > PivotTable > New Worksheet > OK.
Tick fields in the PivotTable Fields pane. Text goes to Rows, numbers go to Values.
Change Sum to Count or Average with Value Field Settings.
When the source data changes, right-click the pivot table and choose Refresh.
requirements: Excel for Mac (Microsoft 365, Excel 2021 or Excel 2024)
Data with one header row and no fully blank rows or columns

steps.name: Tidy your data first
steps.text: Each column needs a header in row 1, like Date, Region, Product and Sales. Remove blank rows inside the range. Pivot tables read the whole block, and a blank row cuts it short.
steps.tip: Press ⌘ + T to turn the range into a table. Tables grow when you add rows, so your pivot table picks up new data on refresh.

steps.name: Click a cell in the data
steps.text: Click any single cell inside the range or table. Excel works out the full range from there.

steps.name: Choose Insert > PivotTable
steps.text: Open the Insert tab on the ribbon and click PivotTable. The Create PivotTable dialog opens with your range or table name already filled in.

steps.name: Pick where the pivot table goes
steps.text: Choose New Worksheet to keep it apart from your data, or Existing Worksheet and click the cell where it should start. Click OK. Excel adds an empty pivot table and opens the PivotTable Fields pane.

steps.name: Tick the fields you want
steps.text: In the PivotTable Fields pane, tick each field to add it. By default, text fields go to Rows, dates go to Columns and numbers go to Values. Drag a field between the Filters, Columns, Rows and Values boxes to change the layout.

steps.name: Change how values are summarized
steps.text: Excel sums numbers by default. To count or average instead, click the small i next to the field in the Values box. You can also right-click a value and choose Value Field Settings. Then pick Count, Average, Max or Min.

shortcuts.action: Turn a range into a table

troubleshooting.problem: "The PivotTable field name is not valid"
troubleshooting.fix: One of your columns has no header. Give every column in row 1 a name, then try Insert > PivotTable again.

troubleshooting.problem: New rows do not show up
troubleshooting.fix: Right-click inside the pivot table and choose Refresh. If rows still go missing, your source is a fixed range. Turn the data into a table (⌘ + T) and point the pivot table at it with PivotTable Analyze > Change Data Source.

troubleshooting.problem: Numbers are counted instead of summed
troubleshooting.fix: The column has text or blank cells mixed in, so Excel treats it as text. Fill the blanks with 0 and make sure the cells are formatted as numbers, then refresh.

blocks.text: A pivot table groups rows that share a value and adds up the numbers for each group. Put Region in Rows and Sales in Values, and you get total sales per region. Add Product to Columns and you get a grid of region by product.

blocks.text: How to refresh a pivot table on Mac

Pivot tables do not update on their own. After you change the source data, right-click anywhere in the pivot table and choose Refresh. To update every pivot table in the workbook, use PivotTable Analyze > Refresh > Refresh All.

faq.question: Where is the PivotTable button in Excel for Mac?
faq.answer: It is on the Insert tab of the ribbon. Click a cell in your data first, then choose Insert > PivotTable.

faq.question: Can I make a pivot table in Numbers instead?
faq.answer: Yes. Numbers for Mac has pivot tables. Select your table, then choose Organize > Create Pivot Table and pick a new or the current sheet. Fields go into Columns, Rows and Values, the same idea as Excel.

faq.question: Why is my pivot table not updating?
faq.answer: Pivot tables only change when you refresh them. Right-click inside it and choose Refresh. If new rows are still missing, change the source to a table so it grows with your data.

faq.question: Can Lazur make the pivot table for me?
faq.answer: Lazur does not click inside Excel for you. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask, and it shows you where each button is, circles it on your screen, and walks you through the steps one click at a time.
